title: Circular Reasoning
skills: recognize circular reasoning in spoken and written arguments
identify when a premise merely restates or assumes the conclusion
distinguish independent evidence from repetitive justification
revise weak arguments by replacing circular claims with relevant support
alignment_note: Provides additional instruction on circular reasoning and how claims can appear supported even when the reasoning simply repeats or assumes the conclusion. Reinforces logical-fallacy recognition, argument evaluation, rhetorical analysis, and evidence-based reasoning across high school English courses.
